messages.author: 9ec69ca07f36d6a1
messages.subject: par called twice per plot?
parts:
In my setup:


spar <- function(mar=if(!axes)
c(2.25+bot-.45*multi,2+left,.5+top+.25*multi,.5+rt)
else
c(3.25+bot-.45*multi,3.5+left,.5+top+.25*multi,.
5+rt),
lwd = if(multi)1 else 1.75,
mgp = if(!axes) mgp=c(.75, .1, 0) else
if(multi) c(1.5, .365, 0) else c(2.4-.4, 0.475,
0),
tcl = if(multi)-0.25 else -0.4,
bot=0, left=0, top=0, rt=0, ps=if(multi) 14 else 10,
mfrow=NULL, axes=TRUE, ...)
{
multi <- length(mfrow) > 0
par(mar=mar, lwd=lwd, mgp=mgp, tcl=tcl, ps=ps, ...)
if(multi) par(mfrow=mfrow)
}

knit_hooks$set(par=function(before, options, envir)
if(before && options$fig.show != 'none')
{
p <-
c('bty','mfrow','ps','bot','top','left','rt','lwd',
'mgp','tcl', 'axes')
pars <- opts_current$get(p)
pars <- pars[!is.na(names(pars))]
if(length(pars)) do.call('spar', pars) else spar()
})

\SweaveOpts{fig.path='titanic-', fig.align='center', w=4.5, h=3.5,
fig.show='hold', fig.lp='fig:titanic-', par=TRUE, tidy=FALSE}

I do thinks like <<myplot,rt=4>>=
rt=4 adds 4 to the default right margin in mar() (done by spar).

But I think I'm seeing spar() called twice per chunk, with the second
call ignoring rt=4. This second call seems to be the one that
matters, so rt is effectively ignored.

Does that make sense? Is there a workaround? Should I be
conditioning on "before" in knit_hooks$set(par=...) ?

Thanks
Frank

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] par called twice per plot?
parts:
You have already conditioned on 'if (before && ...)'. I checked your
par hook, and I saw it was only called once per chunk. It is easy to
verify that by returning a character string in your chunk hook, e.g.

knit_hooks$set(par = function... {
if (...) {
...
return('I was called once...') # this string will be written into tex output
}
})

If it was called twice, you will see two strings in the beginning and
end of a chunk respectively.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: 9ec69ca07f36d6a1
messages.subject: Re: par called twice per plot?
parts:
Thanks Yihui. Returning a character string is a useful debugging
tool. I see the problem now. spar() was being called for every code
chunk even if no plot was produced. I assume that doesn't cause any
problem with graphics rendering for chunks that do produce plots. But
spar() was only called once per chunk, as you said.

I am having a weird problem with the right margin of a graphic being
different with knitr than with a manually run pdf(...)
Here's a small test program if you have time to take a look. The
auxdata argument to dotchart2 in the Hmisc package causes some extra
right margin to be added with par, then right-justifies auxdata in the
right margin. test.pdf is not equal to test2.pdf.

\SweaveOpts{fig.width=4.5, fig.height=3.5}
<<test>>=
require(Hmisc)
# 100 200 300 runs into the figure box right side
dotchart2(1:3, labels=c('a','b','c'), auxdata=(1:3)*100)
@

<<>>=
# Works - 100 200 300 properly set in right margin
pdf('test2.pdf', width=4.5, height=3.5)
require(Hmisc)
dotchart2(1:3, labels=c('a','b','c'), auxdata=(1:3)*100)
dev.off()
@

Thanks again,
Frank

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: par called twice per plot?
parts:
This is somehow expected. To illustrate the problem, you can draw the
plot in an x11() window and resize the window to different sizes. You
will notice the three labels 100, 200 and 300 do not keep a constant
relative distance to the plot frame box: when the plot window is
narrow, they can go inside the plot region. In other words, auxdata
was drawn with a metric that does not scale well.

Now, the problem is knitr records the plot with a null device, of
which the dimension is not clear to me, but I suppose it should be
different with 4.5x3.5 inches. When you save the plot object with the
pdf() device, the labels on the right can be moved to a different
relative location. I'm not sure if Hmisc::outerText can be adjusted to
deal with this situation (e.g. does axis(side = 4) help?).

Regards,
Yihui
--

messages.subject: Re: par called twice per plot?
parts:
That was a huge help Yihui. The dotchart2 and outerText functions
have been problematic for me for years, and I never stopped to think
about text( ) not preserving the right relative location upon
stretching the device window. I re-wrote outerText to use mtext()
instead, and now the right margin text location is preserved under
stretching.

Thanks yet again!
Frank

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: par called twice per plot?
parts:
Someone reported a similar issue about inconsistency of plots with
knitr's recording device and pdf():
https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/157

Now I have found a solution to make them the same with each other by
using the same size in the recording device. The development version
should work (at least with R 2.14.2).

Regards,
Yihui

gets processed into both PDF and HTML versions? Normally I would use
tth or tex4ht as documented here:

http://biostat.mc.vanderbilt.edu/wiki/Main/SweaveConvert#Converting_from_LaTeX_to_html

pandoc and convert to pandoc -> HTML and pandoc -> LaTeX -> PDF, but

applications. I have already got a student.

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr with mk4ht htlatex ? or other Rnw -> tex -> HTML conversion paths
parts:
I guess conversion of complex LaTeX documents is not likely to be
perfect; pandoc is not that smart to recognize all TeX commands. I
tried an Rnw document, the HTML output was just messy, but I guess it
has something to do with the default LaTeX output which uses the
framed package and many home-made commands from the highlight package.
If I use listings output (render_listings()), the conversion seems to
be OK.

Markdown is much simpler and it is almost impossible to write
complicated markdown documents since it is designed to be simple with
only a few common environments.

So for your original post, you can try render_listings() in your first
chunk and see if htlatex works.

Regards,
Yihui
